headline: Discussed camp bus costs, ice rink study, middle school field funding, and Rochford Field contract; no major votes taken.
summary: Karen Bivens reported that five camps and a field trip cost about $30K in buses, against a yearly budget of $70K. Members discussed a $200K cut by the BOE and a $50K allocation by council. The only recorded vote approved the prior meeting minutes unanimously.
decisions: Approved the August 11, 2026 meeting minutes by unanimous vote.

decision_evidence.quote: Chairman Francese made a motion to approve the minutes of the August 11 meeting. Commissioners Mann and Rich Leonardo seconded the motion. The motion was approved by unanimous vote.

plain_text:
TOWN OF HAMDEN, CONNECTICUT 
 
Parks & Recreation Commission 
Minutes         
         
Regular Meeting 
 
7:00 PM, September 8, 2026 
 
 
 
Hamden Government 
Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel:  (203) 287-7070 
Fax:  (203) 287-7075 
 Click to View Agenda   
  
1. CALL TO ORDER 
  
 
• Chairman Francese called the meeting to order at 7:02 PM. 
 
2. ATTENDANCE 
  
 
o In attendance: Dominic Francese, Chair, Arnold Mann, Ryan Ott, Aryn Prestia and Richard 
Leonardo. 
o Absent: Rick Melvin 
• Also in attendance was Anna Montgomery, a member of the public and head coach of the 
Hamden Heronettes artistic swimming team, and Karen Bivens, the Director of Cultural Affairs 
& Human services. 
 
3. APPROVAL OF PREVIOUS MEETING MINUTES 
  
 
 
  1. Approval of August 11, 2026 Minutes  
  
• Chairman Francese made a motion to approve the minutes of the August 11 meeting. 
Commissioners Mann and Rich Leonardo seconded the motion. The motion was approved 
by unanimous vote.  
 
4. PUBLIC COMMENT 
  
 
• Anna Montgomery, resident and head coach of the Hamden Heronettes artistic swimming team 
made public comments concerning pool time availability, the potential for a tuition fee increase, 
and voiced her appreciation of ongoing support.
• Saturday use of the pool is 20% of pool time for the Hamden Artistic team. 
• The Parks and Recs Commission addressed her concern on zoom (link included at the end of 
document) 
 
5. CORRESPONDENCE 
  
 
• (None). 
 
6. EXECUTIVE SESSION 
(if recommended by the town attorney)  
 
• (Not needed). 
 
7. REPORTS 
  
 
 
  1. Director of Cultural Affairs and Human Services, Karen Bivens to briefly report on 
activities of the Parks and Recreation department.  
  • Karen Bivens, Director of Cultural Affairs & Human Services, gave a report on the 
conclusion of camps, the burdening cost of transportation and personnel for the camps, and 
the need to offer an additional field trip, as well as potential increases in cost for camps. 
 
 
o The cost of running 5 camps and a field trip is around $30K in buses. This cost weighs 
heavily on the entire yearly budget of $70K. 
o Commissioner Aryn to make a spreadsheet of the price difference and costs at comparable 
towns. 
• Sensory night taking place this Thursday. 
• The board discussed the $200K cut by the BOE, its effect on Saturday open swim time, the 
$50K allocated by council, and the need for a transparent and itemized list of costs.  
8. OLD BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. Lou Astorino Ice Arena  
  
• Hamden Ice Rink
• The Mayor’s creation of a committee to study the ice rink. Introduction meeting to be held 
this Thursday. 
• Expect a report back from this meeting in our next meeting. 
  
  2. State grant to the town funding - potential parks capital improvements  
  
 
  3. Hamden Middle School Fields  
  
• Middle School Fields 
o The request to allocate funds to improve middle school fields (State Rep spoke to this 
issue).  
o Budget being put together, Karen will check in later this week, but good to know a 
delegation went to view the conditions of the fields.  
o Is there potential to use funds from the Pudicom Trust (currently restricted to plantings). 
 
9. NEW BUSINESS 
  
 
 
  1. BOE Facility use fees for town-sponsored sports leagues  
  
 
  2. Rochford Field contract  
  • Rochford Field Contract 
o Commissioners discussed how much the fields are used and the cost to outside 
organizations. 
o The Mayor’s ask to Albertus and whether we could include the free use of the 
pool to this discussion 
o Commissioner Ryan will draft something to address the ongoing discussion with 
Albertus.  
  3. League stipends  
  • Sport league stipends 
o There is a need to have proper financial documents on the issue of stipends. 
o The Chair will email leagues to get names, insurance, and seek answers to the 
three questions on: demographics, risk management and names of those 
participating.  
  4. HHS Tennis court repair  
  • Hamden Tennis courts 
o Getting closer to our funding stack goals, however this is a moving target because 
of inflation   
10. ADJOURNMENT
• The Chair motioned to adjourn the meeting at 9:02PM, it was seconded by Commissioner Mann. 
The vote to adjourn was unanimous.
